subject: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenark.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time last week. Our consumption audit for GreenArk’s account shows a ~28% uplift in inference-hours for May (vs. committed baseline) driven by two short-lived model evaluation projects and a mid-month spike on the ingest pipeline. I’ve attached the CSV extract from the audit and a concise proposal PDF that maps how we recommend settling the retroactive usage and aligning the remainder of the term to avoid repeated true-ups.

High-level proposal: 
- One-time settlement for the May delta (usage-based charge) with a 30-day due window.
- Apply a portion (20%) of the one-time charge as an upfront credit toward an agreed capacity uplift (adds 10% committed capacity) for the remaining 6 months.
- Formalize a short amendment to the SOW to reflect the uplift and updated unit rates.

Next steps I suggest: if this approach looks sensible, I’ll loop in Marcus (finance) to finalize numbers and Laura to draft the amendment + DocuSign.

Attachments: greenark-usage-audit-202705.csv, settlement-proposal-20270608.pdf

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0186

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenark.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2

Thanks Mina — quick clarifying questions before we loop others in: 
1) Can you provide a day-by-day breakout for the May spike and identify if any of the traffic is attributable to our internal load tests (we ran some in mid-May)?
2) For the credit toward uplift, will the uplift pricing be based on our current committed rate or the volume-discounted tier if we go further (we may want to accelerate to 20% uplift).
3) We’ll need a simple invoice for accounting showing the one-time charge and the applied credit.

If possible, can you get Marcus in copy with the settlement numbers so we can get a PO issued early next week?

— Alex
Alex Chen
Director, ML Platforms
GreenArk Labs
alex.chen@greenark.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenark.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@greenark.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2

Appreciate the questions, Alex. Looping in Marcus (finance) and Laura (AM) to confirm the numbers and next steps. Answers inline below and Marcus will attach the reconciliation workbook: 

1) Day-by-day breakout: see attached reconciliation-sheet-20270610.xlsx — the spike is concentrated on May 11–13 and May 21. The May 11–13 window aligns with the internal load-test you mentioned; we’ve separated that traffic in tab "test_vs_prod". The remaining uplift is production traffic (primarily longer sequences).

2) Uplift pricing: You’ll keep your current committed unit rate for the 10% bridging uplift. If you accelerate to 20% today, we can apply the next discount tier — Marcus will list both scenarios in the sheet.

3) Invoice: Marcus will produce a one-line settlement invoice showing gross charge, applied uplift credit, and net payable.

Marcus/Laura — can you confirm the net figures and provide invoice + amendment draft? Alex/Samantha — happy to run a 15-min call if you prefer to walk through the workbook live.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenark.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@greenark.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2

Hi all — attached is the reconciliation-sheet-20270610.xlsx with the numbers pulled from billing and our internal audit. Summary (rounded): 
- Gross retroactive May delta: $28,740.00
- Applied uplift credit (20% of gross if you take the 10% committed uplift): $5,748.00
- Net one-time payable: $22,992.00

Alternative: accelerate to 20% committed uplift and the applied credit increases to $8,622.00 with a net payable of $20,118.00. 

Invoice + amendment: I’ve prepared a one-line pro forma invoice and a short amendment draft in the shared HubSpot deal (link below). Alex — if you can confirm which uplift option you want, I’ll issue an invoice (Net 30) and route the amendment to DocuSign.

Attachments: reconciliation-sheet-20270610.xlsx
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54321

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Financial Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@greenark.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Settlement proposal and capacity uplift — usage recast for Q2

Thanks Marcus — GreenArk will take the accelerated path and commit to 20% uplift for the remaining 6 months. Please send the pro forma invoice for $20,118.00 and the amendment to DocuSign. We aim to get this on PO/finance queue today.

Samantha, I’ve copied you to confirm procurement will approve the PO once the DocuSign counter-signed amendment is available.

Best,
Alex
